title: Adaptive Phase Granulator: mediator for dynamic prefill/decode splitpoints
creator: Leah Gomez
description:
Problem statement: Current prefill/decode scheduling uses static phase split heuristics that either favor throughput (coarser batches, longer prefill windows) or latency (finer splits, isolated decode slots). These rules do not adapt to cross-tenant attention-cost characteristics or to changing kernel selection benefits (e.g., sparse-attn fastpaths on certain sequence ranges). As a result we observe tail latency spikes under mixed workloads and suboptimal GPU utilization for attention-heavy prompts.

Goal: Implement an in-runtime mediator — the Adaptive Phase Granulator (APG) — which dynamically selects phase splitpoints per-request using a lightweight attention-cost estimator, kernel speedup hints, and tenant SLO constraints. The APG should make fine-grained tradeoffs between latency and throughput while preserving fairness across tenants and avoiding starvation of low-priority requests.
background: We have many existing experiments (prefill splitters, hedged routing, kernel probing) but they are static or tenant-grouped. Benchmark traces from Jan-Feb show 18% tail latency regression for tenant mixes with high-attention initial prompts. Kernel selection improvements (quantized sparse kernels) provide variable speedups depending on sequence-length and head-density; this information is not surfaced to the scheduler. Product wants bounded p99 latency regressions for Premium customers while improving average throughput for best-effort tenants.
proposed_solution:
APG components: 1) Lightweight Attention Cost Estimator that ingests prompt metadata (length, approximate head-density signal if available, tokenization features) and returns a 1-5 compute-cost score. 2) Kernel Speedup Hint Registry: table of model variant + sequence window -> expected speedup for candidate kernels. Populated by offline profiler and online probes. 3) Splitpoint Optimizer: for each incoming request, compute candidate splitpoints (no-split, early-split, multi-split) and simulate expected latency and throughput using short cost model. Select splitpoint that meets tenant SLO and maximizes aggregate utilization with fairness weight. 4) Fairness Weight Adjuster enforces tenant share by soft-penalizing repeated demotions and tracking recent service ratio. 5) Fallback and hedging policy for probe-mismatch.

Implementation notes: implement estimator as a small Rust module within the scheduler hot path (per-request < 250us). Kernel hint registry served from local cache updated every 5 minutes. Use an A/B experiment harness to route 10% of traffic initially.

Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency per-tier, GPU utilization, tokens/s, fairness violation rate (requests starved > threshold), fallback rate.

acceptance_criteria: APG decision added to request trace and can be toggled via runtime flag
No more than 5% regression in p99 for Premium tier compared to baseline under canary mix
Tokens/s increased by at least 6% for best-effort tenants on mixed workload traces
Fairness violation rate under 0.5% (requests starved longer than SLA threshold)
Fallback/hedge rate below 2% when kernel-probing indicates mismatch
Unit and integration tests for estimator and registry with >= 90% branch coverage

decisions: Estimator implemented in Rust in scheduler hotpath to meet latency constraints
Kernel hint registry served locally with 5-minute TTL and periodic offline updates
Fairness is soft-weighted; no hard preemption of ongoing decodes during canary
Canary rollout at 10% traffic with auto-rollback if Premium p99 regresses beyond 5%
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: estimator mispredicts attention cost -> mitigation: hedged early-split fallback and probe after split
Risk: kernel hint staleness -> mitigation: online probe sampling and per-request fallback to conservative kernel
Risk: fairness accounting overhead -> mitigation: approximate counting with sliding window sketch

Latency panel: p50/p95/p99 split by decision type and kernel chosen
Utilization panel: tokens/s and GPU occupancy for A/B groups
Alert: Premium p99 regression > 5% for 15m -> auto-disable APG canary
